report.title: 2025 Water Quality Report - NASA Ames Research Center, Moffett Field, California (July 2026)
report.sources_described: Drinking water at NASA Ames is supplied by the San Francisco Regional Water System (SFRWS), owned and operated by the SFPUC: Hetch Hetchy surface water (unfiltered; UV and chlorine disinfection, pH adjustment, fluoridation, chloramination) plus Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant filtered water; upcountry non-Hetch Hetchy sources and groundwater wells were not used in 2025, and the SFRWS imported a very small amount (0.38%) of treated water from Valley Water in April and May 2025. NASA Ames does not use groundwater.
violations: No exceedances of drinking water standards were identified in any of the samples collected at NASA Ames in 2025 (page 3; footnote 1: all results met State and Federal drinking water health standards).

Monitoring violation disclosed on behalf of the supplier (page 3): the San Francisco Regional Water System, operated by SFPUC, failed to monitor for recycled filter backwash water turbidity at its Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant from June 23, 2025 to July 2, 2025 because of a turbidimeter equipment failure; corrected July 3, 2025; the SFPUC states it was not an emergency and did not impact water quality.

Lead and copper tap monitoring (page 5, footnote 7): in the September 2023 round, 2 of 22 site samples (Buildings M583C and N200) had lead above the Action Level of 15 ppb; the 90th percentile (10.4 ppb) was below the AL so no regulatory violation occurred. N200 fountains are fitted with NSF/ANSI-certified lead-removing filters; M583C is abandoned and scheduled for demolition.

report.title: 2025 City of Milpitas Water Quality Report
report.sources_described: The City of Milpitas delivers treated water from two wholesale sources, the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC, Hetch Hetchy water combined with treated local water from Calaveras and San Antonio Reservoirs via the Sunol Valley WTP) and Valley Water (Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta and local Anderson/Calero reservoir water treated at the Penitencia and Santa Teresa WTPs), both delivering treated surface water. Under normal conditions the two supplies are kept separate and not blended; an emergency groundwater well (Pinewood Well) is a backup.
violations: Page 1: 'In Calendar Year 2025, your water met all USEPA and State drinking water health standards. We are proud to report that our system had no water quality standard violations.'

Page 13 (printed 11), monitoring violation: 'We are required to monitor your drinking water for specific contaminants on a regular basis. Results of regular monitoring are an indicator of whether or not your drinking water meets health standards. During May 2025, we did not complete all monitoring for coliform bacteria, and therefore, cannot be sure of the quality of your drinking water during that time.'
report.extraction_notes: Data tables are on PDF pages 12-13 (printed page numbers 10-11; printed page n = PDF page n+2). Table columns: 'Distribution System', 'Valley Water' (note b: fed by Santa Teresa and Penitencia WTPs) and 'SFPUC'; one entry per analyte per column that has a value, source_group = column name. Source-water rows have only Valley Water and SFPUC values; lead/copper, disinfectant residual, TTHM, HAA5 and total coliform are single distribution-system values (source_group 'Distribution System'). Where the Average cell is ND or '<x' but the Range has a numeric high, value = range high with value_basis 'range high', average null, detected true. ND, '<3', '<6', '<20', '<0.1' range-lows are recorded as 0 with the printed form in notes. MCL/AL/MRDL/ORL strings are copied as printed, including parentheses '(15)', brackets '[4]' and '1000 (NL)'. Non-regulated table has an 'ORL' column instead of MCL; it is stored in mcl_printed. Secondary and non-regulated tables have no PHG column (phg_printed null). Specific conductance unit printed 'µS/cm', stored as 'uS/cm'. pH unit printed as a dash; SFPUC pH printed '-' and omitted. Lead 90th percentile printed as 0.0025 ppb (copied exactly; possibly a units slip in the report). Turbidity primary rows: Range column holds a percent-of-time figure, not a range. Uranium note e says radioactive monitoring is every nine years (detected 2013), so sample_year is null for uranium. PDF page 10 (printed 8, 'How to Read the Water Quality Table') shows a faded, cut-off sample table whose values differ from the 2025 table (e.g. Bromate 2.45 / 2.1c, Fluoride ND / 0.4, TOC 2.5 / 1.8, Turbidity 0.28 / 0.4c) and appears to be an earlier year's layout example; those rows were NOT extracted. UCMR 5 results are stated only in text (page 9: no detections 2022-2025 for 29 PFAS plus lithium); two text-derived detected:false entries were added and flagged in notes. Individual-result exceedances inside ranges (HAA5 range high 75.0 ppb vs MCL 60; distribution turbidity range high 30 NTU vs SMCL 5; distribution odor range high 40 TON vs SMCL 3) are noted on the entries; the report declares no violations.

report.extraction_notes: Single-source (groundwater) system; tables have one results column, so source_group is null throughout. The report's results column is headed 'Amount Detected' (or 'Detected') with a separate 'Range Low-High' column; Amount Detected is treated as the average (value_basis 'average', average filled) except where the row itself names another basis (90th percentile for lead/copper, annual running average for free chlorine, highest monthly percent positive for total coliform). Leading-dot numbers (.15, .11, .0027, .38, .015, .23, .0046) are stored as decimals; ND range-lows are stored as 0. PFHxS average is printed ',0073' (comma) and stored as 0.0073. Iron is printed in ppm (SMCL 0.3 ppm) and lead/copper in ppm; units are kept as printed. pH has no printed unit. Specific conductance unit printed 'µS/cm', stored as 'uS/cm'. Disinfection by-products appear in two sub-tables: 'Calero Pressure Zone Only' (TTHM, HAA, free chlorine; Range 'None') on page 2 and per-site rows (#4, #5, #9, #10, #17, #18 TTHM/HAA) on page 3; each row is a separate entry with the site in raw_name/notes. The 'Other Substances' table (alkalinity, bicarbonate, calcium, hardness, magnesium, potassium, sodium) has no MCL/PHG columns. Lead and copper were sampled in 2023 (year printed in the table); all other rows 2025. No E. coli, radon, VOC, or secondary manganese/zinc rows are printed (report lists detected contaminants only).
